Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

Duplicate of #32548 — same root cause (MAX_STEPS_PROMPT sent as assistant prefill), same 400. Tracking there; fix PR #34276 already open.

Still reproduces on 1.18.3, and the injection line is unchanged on dev. Hit it twice, each at exactly the agent's configured step ceiling, with all prior steps succeeding:

- claude-sonnet-5 subagent, `steps: 40`, thinking variant (max) → 400 on step 40
- claude-opus-4-8 subagent, `steps: 200`, thinking variant (xhigh) → 400 on step 200

#34276 (send as `user` role instead of assistant prefill) is the right fix — the wrap-up message is useful, the model just needs to be allowed to answer it.
Seems silly to close an active issue without fixing it.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

**Related PR Found:**

- **#35777** — `fix(core): refresh stale @latest npm package cache on load`  
  https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/35777

This PR is directly related. According to the PR description, #37688 builds on #35777 by addressing the same issue (stale `@latest` plugin cache) but improves the error handling. #35777 threw `InstallFailedError` when the refresh `reify` failed, breaking the plugin load. PR #37688 wraps that refresh in `Effect.catch` to fall back to the cache instead, making the refresh attempt non-breaking even if the registry is temporarily unavailable.

Root cause is now deterministic: V2 rejects a relative target such as `../sibling/file` before `external_directory` permission evaluation, unlike V1. The nested path error also has an empty message, which explains the blank UI error. #37689 restores the V1-compatible permission flow and adds patch-level regression coverage. The malformed empty tool calls are separate from this path failure and remain tracked by #36766 and #37159.
Thanks for updating your PR! It now meets our contributing guidelines. :+1:

Confirming this on the **desktop app** (macOS, OpenCode Desktop 1.18.3, `ai.opencode.desktop`) — with an extra wrinkle: in the desktop app the stale path lives in **two** places, and the second one poisons every launch.

1. `session.directory` (same as this issue) — sessions bound to a deleted Superset worktree subfolder (`/Users/robert/.superset/worktrees/540f8918-…/test-setup`, removed when the worktree was cleaned up).
2. The app`'s persisted global state `~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop/opencode.global.dat` → `server.projects.local[].worktree` and `server.lastProject.local`, both still pointing at the deleted path.

What I observed:

- At every app launch the sidecar calls `FileSystem.realPath(lastProject)` from inside `Server.listen` and dies with `PlatformError: NotFound … ENOENT` (stack in `app.asar/out/main/chunks/node-*.js`).
- `GET /api/reference?directory=<deleted>` → HTTP 500.
- Every `POST /session/{id}/prompt_async` for those sessions fails with `Cause([Die(PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (…))])` — 200+ occurrences in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`. As analyzed above, the `Die` bypasses the `BadRequest` mapping, so the client gets a 500 at best.
- The chat UI shows **no error at all**: the message appears to send and the session just never responds. The error only lands in the app`'s notification store as a toast, nothing in-chat.
- The project name displayed in the UI is derived from the git root (the main repo), so from the user`'s perspective they are "in the main project on the main worktree" while the session is actually bound to the deleted worktree subfolder — there is no way to see which worktree path a session is bound to.
- The broken state persists across restarts with no recovery path in the UI; the only fix was removing the dead entry from `opencode.global.dat` / the stale sessions from the DB by hand.

Building on the root-cause analysis above, I`'d suggest:
- Validate `projects[].worktree` / `lastProject` at app boot and drop or flag missing paths **before** the sidecar resolves them.
- When `prompt_async` dies this way, surface a session-level error in the chat UI (the event stream already carries enough to detect it).
- Show the bound directory/worktree per session in the UI so stale bindings are visible.

Another data point, this time on **macOS** (Desktop 1.18.3) — so not WSL-specific. Same failure family: `opencode.global.dat` + stale absolute paths.

What happened here: a Superset worktree subfolder (`/Users/robert/.superset/worktrees/540f8918-…/test-setup`) was deleted out from under the app. The app kept it in the `server` key of `opencode.global.dat`:

```json
"projects": { "local": [
  { "worktree": "…/test-setup", "expanded": true },
  { "worktree": "/Users/robert/Documents/Default Project", "expanded": true }
]},
"lastProject": { "local": "…/test-setup" }
```

Symptoms:

- Every launch: sidecar `realpath(lastProject)` inside `Server.listen` → `PlatformError: NotFound … ENOENT`; `/api/reference?directory=<deleted>` → HTTP 500.
- Every send in the affected sessions: `prompt_async failed` with `Cause([Die(PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (…))])` — and **no error in the chat UI**. The message appears to send; the session never responds.
- Renderer console stays clean (only ResizeObserver noise). The failure is only visible in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` and the app`'s Chromium netlog (`…/T/ai.opencode.desktop.scoped_dir.*/event_file_*.json`).
- The UI derives the displayed project from the git root, so the dead worktree path is invisible — it looks like "the main project is broken", and selecting the main worktree doesn`'t help because new sessions were still being created against `lastProject`.

Strong +1 on the repair-path suggestions: in this state there is no in-app way to fix or even diagnose it — I had to inspect the netlog and sqlite DBs to find the binding. Boot-time validation of `projects[].worktree` / `lastProject` (drop-or-flag missing) plus an in-chat error when `prompt_async` dies would have made this a 30-second fix.

Had the same issue. Actually fired up Opencode CLI w/ GLM 5.2 and asked it to solve it.

Ultimately, after a lot of work it came down the following line:

`/opt/OpenCode/ai.opencode.desktop --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --ozone-platform=x11`

I haven't found a way to make it work without `--no-sandbox`.

Below is the documentation that it generated to explain what it found:

## Summary

OpenCode Desktop (v1.18.3) appeared to do nothing when launched from the desktop shortcut on Ubuntu 25.10 running under VMware. Investigation revealed a combination of GPU-process crash and Wayland compositor incompatibility specific to VMware's SVGA II graphics adapter. The fix was to launch the Electron app with GPU disabled, the Chromium sandbox off, and XWayland (X11) instead of native Wayland.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Ubuntu 25.10 |
| Desktop | GNOME on Wayland |
| Hypervisor | VMware (SVGA II Adapter) |
| CPU | Intel i9-9900K (passed through to VM) |
| Display | 1920x1080 |
| OpenCode Desktop | 1.18.3 (installed via `.deb` at `/opt/OpenCode/`) |
| OpenCode CLI | `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` (working) |

## Symptoms

- Clicking the desktop shortcut produced no visible window.
- No error output appeared (the `.desktop` file sets `Terminal=false`).
- `opencode-desktop` was not on `PATH`, so running it from a terminal returned "command not found."
- The CLI (`opencode`) worked fine — only the desktop app was affected.

## Root Cause

Three separate problems combined to make the window never appear:

1. **GPU-process SIGILL crash.** A crash report existed at
   `/var/crash/_opt_OpenCode_ai.opencode.desktop.1000.crash` with `Signal: 4`
   (SIGILL — Illegal Instruction). Chromium's VA-API video decoder path fails
   against VMware's virtual GPU:
   ```
   ERROR:media/gpu/vaapi/vaapi_wrapper.cc:1658] vaInitialize failed: unknown libva error
   ```
   On some launches the GPU process crashes hard (SIGILL); on others it logs
   the VA-API error but keeps running.

2. **Wayland window never maps.** With the GPU process disabled, the main
   process and renderer stayed alive (9 stable processes, sidecar server
   ready, renderer loading `oc://renderer/assets/*.js`) but no window appeared
   on screen. `xdotool`/`wmctrl` found no window, and GNOME Shell's window
   list was empty. This is a known class of issue with Electron apps under
   VMware's Wayland pipeline.

3. **Window only shows on `ready-to-show`.** The app's main process creates the
   `BrowserWindow` with `show: false` and only calls `win.show()` inside the
   `ready-to-show` event handler (see `out/main/index.js` around line 1271).
   When the renderer stalls or the compositor never acknowledges the surface,
   `ready-to-show` never fires and the window stays invisible forever.

   Window-state JSON (`~/.config/ai.opencode.desktop/window-state-*.json`) was
   valid (1280x800 at 342,159 on a 1920x1080 display) — **not** an
   off-screen/corrupted-position problem.

## Diagnosis Steps

1. **Found the binary and crash report:**
   ```bash
   dpkg -l | grep opencode            # → opencode 1.18.3 amd64
   find / -iname '*opencode*' ...     # → /opt/OpenCode/ai.opencode.desktop
                                      # → /var/crash/_opt_OpenCode_...1000.crash
   ```

2. **Read the crash report:**
   ```bash
   grep -aE '^(Signal|ExecutablePath|Date):' /var/crash/_opt_OpenCode_...crash
   # Signal: 4   ← SIGILL
   ```

3. **Ran the binary directly to see live output:**
   ```bash
   /opt/OpenCode/ai.opencode.desktop --version
   # → app starting { version: '1.18.3' }
   # → ERROR:media/gpu/vaapi/vaapi_wrapper.cc:1658 vaInitialize failed
   ```

4. **Inspected the desktop entry the shortcut uses:**
   ```bash
   cat /usr/share/applications/opencode-desktop.desktop
   # Exec=/opt/OpenCode/ai.opencode.desktop %U
   ```

5. **Verified saved window state was sane** (ruled out off-screen window).

6. **Extracted `app.asar` to read the window-creation logic** and confirmed
   `

The additional symptom you've identified (already-completed parallel tool calls remaining `running` while the processor waits on `Permission.ask`) adds a new angle beyond what those issues cover, so if you feel this is distinct enough, feel free to leave it open for maintainer review.

Well, I wrote a reverse proxy for LM Studio, though it can be used with any other LLM server (it requires a fork).

With this reverse proxy, I can identify the OpenCode sub-agent session and manage concurrency.
If anyone is interested, here it is: https://github.com/fernandoglatz/openai-compatible-proxy
